priorStories.headline: Hurricane Trudy threatens Mexico’s Pacific coast
priorStories.body:
Hurricane Trudy was affecting west-central Mexico’s Pacific coast as a Category 2 storm, with sustained winds of 100 mph.

A hurricane warning covered the coast from Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes. The U.S. National Hurricane Center warned of dangerous storm surge and damaging waves along with flooding and mudslides.

priorStories.headline: French protests draw 550,000, with 400 arrests
priorStories.body:
About 550,000 people joined 110 marches over living costs and school conditions, according to France’s interior minister. Organizers estimated attendance at 800,000.

Authorities reported roughly 400 arrests after clashes, fires and looting in several cities. An investigation was opened after a protester in Saint-Etienne lost a hand.

priorStories.headline: Romanian jets shoot down two attack drones
priorStories.body:
Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Geran attack drones after they entered the country’s airspace over its territorial waters, Romania’s Defence Ministry said.

The drones were downed southeast and east of Sulina. The ministry said one spent two minutes in Romanian airspace and the other five minutes.

priorStories.headline: Kolkata festival crowd crush kills at least 19
priorStories.body:
At least 19 people died and 25 were injured in a crowd crush at a Durga Puja pavilion in north Kolkata, officials said.

The crush occurred Saturday night as people near the religious festival site sought shelter from rain.

candidates.summary: An overnight Ukrainian drone attack caused fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal, the Ruchi oil depot and other sites in and around St. Petersburg, Russian officials said. Governor Alexander Beglov reported one person killed and five wounded. Russia’s Defense Ministry said air defenses destroyed 1,015 drones across multiple regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea; the claims were not independently verified.
candidates.title: Drone attack ignites fires at St. Petersburg oil sites

candidates.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said Sunday that the number of arrests arising from Saturday’s nationwide protests had risen to 1,800. He also said more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters had been injured and that the casualty count remained provisional. The update substantially revised figures reported Saturday night.
candidates.title: France raises protest arrest count to 1,800

candidates.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection in Israel’s October 27 election. Netanyahu thanked Trump in a statement issued by his Likud party. The endorsement followed months in which Trump had declined to explicitly back Netanyahu’s campaign.
candidates.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu for reelection

candidates.summary: Pope Leo XIV appeared at the Apostolic Palace window for the traditional Sunday Angelus, four days after surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung because of a malignant tumor. He thanked those who prayed for him and said he would gradually resume his duties. The surgery confirmed adenocarcinoma.
candidates.title: Pope Leo says he will gradually resume duties

candidates.summary: French authorities said Sunday that at least 1,800 people had been arrested following Saturday’s nationwide protests. Hundreds of demonstrators gathered again at Paris’ Place de la République, where police used tear gas as tensions flared. President Emmanuel Macron scheduled an emergency meeting and an evening address. The Interior Ministry previously said more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured.
candidates.title: France raises protest arrest count to 1,800

candidates.summary: French authorities raised the number of arrests following Saturday’s nationwide protests to at least 2,400. In a televised address Sunday, President Emmanuel Macron condemned the rioting and looting, blamed much of the violence on radical far-left groups and said those responsible would be held accountable. Police again used tear gas as demonstrators gathered in Paris.
candidates.title: France raises protest arrest count to 2,400

candidates.summary: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security said Ukrainians and Sudanese enrolled in Temporary Protected Status would retain protection from deportation while final decisions about their programs remain pending. The protections, covering tens of thousands of Ukrainians and hundreds of Sudanese nationals, had been scheduled to terminate Monday.
candidates.title: U.S. temporarily retains protections for Ukrainians and Sudanese

candidates.summary: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said 39 people remained hospitalized after Saturday’s fast-moving fire at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, including at least 19 in critical condition, some with severe burns. Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed four service members were killed. Canada’s Defence Department said the fire began in the base’s training area and spread beyond its boundaries; the cause remained under investigation.
candidates.title: Alberta says 39 hospitalized after military base fire

Wade Rutland said military officials knew about the grass fire for hours and believed it was sufficiently contained for live-fire training to continue before winds shifted, sending flames about one kilometer in 36 seconds. Four soldiers from the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry, were killed. Of 39 injured people, 19 were critical, eight stable and 12 ambulatory. Investigators had not determined what ignited the fire.
candidates.title: Military details rapid spread of deadly Wainwright fire

candidates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said U.S. intelligence sharing used to warn Ukraine about incoming Russian ballistic missiles was working again after being blocked for several days. President Donald Trump had previously said the United States had not stopped sharing intelligence.
candidates.title: Zelenskyy says U.S. intelligence sharing has resumed

candidates.summary: A drone crossed Lithuania after apparently entering from Poland, prompting air alerts and the deployment of NATO fighters before it came down in the northern Pasvalys district. Debris damaged the door of a moving car, but no one was injured. Ukraine apologized and said Russian electronic warfare may have diverted the drone during an operation against targets in Russia; Lithuanian authorities were investigating its route and origin.
candidates.title: Drone crosses Lithuania and damages moving car

candidates.summary: A Saudi AH-6i reconnaissance helicopter crashed in the Najran region, killing its two National Guard officer crew members. The Saudi-led coalition attributed the crash to a technical malfunction. Yemen’s Houthis separately claimed they had shot down a Saudi Apache helicopter near the border; the coalition rejected that account.
candidates.title: Saudi military helicopter crash kills two officers

stories.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the United States had restored intelligence sharing used to warn Ukraine about incoming Russian ballistic missiles after blocking it for several days.

President Donald Trump had previously said the United States never stopped sharing intelligence, leaving the duration and circumstances of any interruption disputed.
stories.headline: U.S. resumes missile warnings for Ukraine

stories.body:
An overnight Ukrainian drone attack caused fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal, the Ruchi oil depot and other locations around St. Petersburg, according to Russian officials. The regional governor reported one person killed and five wounded.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said air defenses destroyed 1,015 drones across several regions, occupied Crimea and the Black Sea. That unusually large count was not independently verified, and the extent of damage or disruption at the oil facilities was not disclosed.
stories.headline: Drone attacks hit St. Petersburg oil sites

stories.body:
French authorities raised the number of arrests following Saturday’s nationwide protests from roughly 400 to at least 2,400.

President Emmanuel Macron condemned the rioting and looting in a televised address Sunday, blaming much of the violence on radical far-left groups. Police again used tear gas as demonstrators gathered in Paris.
stories.headline: French protest arrests rise to 2,400

stories.body:
The Department of Homeland Security said Ukrainians and Sudanese enrolled in Temporary Protected Status will remain protected from deportation while the government makes final decisions about their programs.

The protections, which had been scheduled to end Monday, cover tens of thousands of Ukrainians and hundreds of Sudanese nationals.
stories.headline: U.S. extends deportation protection for two groups

stories.body:
Four Canadian soldiers were killed and 39 people were injured when a grass fire spread rapidly during live-fire training at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta. Nineteen of the injured were in critical condition.

Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland said officials had known about the fire for hours but believed it was sufficiently contained to continue training. After winds shifted, the flames traveled about one kilometer in 36 seconds. Investigators had not determined how the fire started.
stories.headline: Canadian base fire kills four soldiers
